thread:
carla_finance: Heads up 1: invoice INV-2026-03-09 for ACME shows 40,032,000 embedding units for Feb 20-21; ledger shows ~4,003,200. Possible double-count or unit error.

maya_billing: Yikes. Checking export/backfill logs now.

billing-bot: backfill-job #bfill-emb-20260309 started at 2026-03-09T03:02:12Z

arjun_backend: Metering DB query returns 4,003,200 units (matches ledger). Looks like exporter produced X10.

maya_billing: Found exporter CSV row: embedding_units=40032000. Exporter config `normalization_factor` was set to 10 in deploy 2026-03-09T02:58.

carla_finance: Root cause noted: exporter multiplier bug. Plan: 1) void/reissue invoice, 2) issue credit memo, 3) re-export dry-run, 4) add alert for large export deltas.

kevin_cfo: Approve credit/adjustment up to $48k. Loop me if > threshold.

arjun_backend: Ran dry-run: `billing export reprocess --customer acme --start 2026-02-20 --end 2026-02-21 --dry-run` -> embedding_units=4,003,200. I pushed a quick exporter assert (norm_factor==1) to staging and added a reconciliation job to flag >1.5x mismatches.

maya_billing: Created INV-2026-03-09-R1 and credit memo CM-2026-03-09-ACME with corrected embedding_units=4,003,200. Sending to customer now.

jon_sales: Drafting customer note: "We found an internal billing export bug that multiplied embedding usage by 10 for Feb 20-21. We've issued a corrected invoice and credit memo. Apologies for the inconvenience."

carla_finance: Approved. Finance will sweep other invoices in that deploy window. Keep updates here.

jon_sales: Customer reply: "Thanks for the quick fix 1 appreciate the transparency." :pray:
